-world problem-solving has given rise to complex numerical challenges that demand efficient high-order numerical methods. These methods can be categorized into local methods, which involve solving discrete equations within a specific domain, and global methods that solve equations across the entire problem space. Local methods are typically non-interfering, enabling the parallel processing of problems on diverse hardware systems, whereas global methods are characterized by extensive data communication requirements that impede parallel processing. Although local methods are characterized by straightforward implementation and management, they are limited by small local stencils and can result in the generation of large sparse matrices that are difficult to solve iteratively. In contrast, global methods are characterized by relatively smaller dense matrices that are more readily solvable. In an effort to leverage the simplicity of global methods and the modularity of local methods, a new approach is presented in this paper that involves employing a block-diagonalization technique to transform a large sparse matrix into a collection of smaller dense matrices that can be solved simultaneously, thus providing a hybrid approach that combines the best features of both local and global methods.

The true reward is defined as the difference between the received reward and the reported reward. 
In this study, we model deceptive reinforcement learning where the state and reward distortions are bounded in magnitude, 
and the sum of the distortions in the reward is bounded in magnitude over time. 
In a deceptive MDP without bounded state distortions, an optimal policy is always identifiable. 
Our analysis shows that, when both the state and reward are limited in influence, optimal policies are still obtainable 
with reinforcement learning within an additional bounded error term that depends on the magnitude of the reward distortion bound. 
The proposed technique for achieving this involves constructing and executing a policy on a modified MDP that mimics the MDP with bounded state distortions, 
resulting in an additional bounded error term that exclusively relies on the bounded reward distortion bound. 
The stated bounds are likely not the most efficient, but we establish a significant improvement over the prior bound for MDPs with bounded state distortions.

al Neural Networks (GCNNs), have gained significant popularity in processing complex and irregular data patterns. GCNNs have demonstrated superior performance in various tasks, including node, edge, and whole graph-level tasks. However, most existing GCNNs focus on structured graphs, neglecting the dynamic changes in graph data, which can significantly impact their performance. In this study, we introduce a new class of time-dependent GCNNs, called Time-Dependent Graph Convolutional Autoencoders (TDGCAE). The new model extends traditional GCNNs to capture the dynamic relationships in graph data by incorporating a autoencoder structure and a Kullback-Leibler divergence loss function. Our experiments show that the TDGCAE model outperforms existing models in reconstructing hidden graph structures and predicting future graph structures, making it a valuable tool for analyzing complex and dynamic graph data.

gravity can be redefined in terms of first-order Christoffel symbols and their associated Hamiltonian mechanics. The CHS-Einstein duality in three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space allows us to define the higher-spin Einstein static universe as a stable configuration surrounding this space. Perturbations of this static universe can be mapped to a CHS vacuum and its Hilbert Hilbert Hilbert space, consisting of hs(3, R) representations, and the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of an eternal Einstein static universe is shown to be equivalent to the entanglement entropy of a thermal state in this Hilbert space. Furthermore, we can construct a dual CHS boundary conformal field theory, and its version of entanglement entropy coincides with the thermal entanglement entropy in the hs(3, C) boundary CHS Hilbert space.

a new version of the Grandfather Paradox is introduced, where a time traveler prevents their own birth by taking a specific action in the past. Specifically, we investigate how these techniques generalize across different domains and speech patterns when speech is limited. We focus on speech rate variations, comparing fast, normal, and slow speech. Our analysis primarily involves the Librispeech dataset, with some cross-dataset testing using the Voxpopuli speech dataset. The results show that deep learning speech models generally perform better when trained and evaluated on data with similar speech rates. However, they can still achieve reasonable performance when evaluating on data with different speech rates. The results also reveal that these systems do not exhibit distinct specialization for different speech rates, indicating that they do not overfit these patterns. This suggests that speech rate is not as significant of a distinguishing feature as other factors like accent or gender. Despite these positive outcomes, the performance of limited data speech models is still lower compared to state-of-the-end results. This indicates that there is room for improvement in speech rate invariance within current speech recognition systems.

To address this, it is common practice to use sparsity-inducing priors under the assumption that the target image can be represented efficiently using certain bases. However, this approach has limitations, particularly when the target image has rich textures that are difficult to represent with few coefficients. To overcome this, recent studies have explored self-representation based methods, notably coherent subspace fitting, which has been proven to enjoy stable solutions and guarantees. Despite its benefits, these methods are computationally demanding due to the high complexity of solving related linear systems. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel formulation that rephrases the coefficient matrix construction as an optimal control problem, allowing us to substitute the sparsity-inducing prior with a more robust $\ell_2$-norm. This substitution not only reduces computational costs, but also retains certain mathematical properties of the original method, such as stability and convergence to a well-defined solution. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our proposed technique achieves comparable results to the original method with significantly improved efficiency.

, the gauge-fixing procedure results in a set of four constraints that impose restrictions on the gravitational perturbation. However, the existing formulation of these constraints does not clearly indicate how many degrees of freedom the gravity field actually possesses. To remedy this ambiguity, a novel gauge condition has been developed in this article, incorporating a reparametrization of the constraint equations. This new condition reverts to its standard harmonic gauge form once the unique solution to the reparametrized equations is incorporated. Consequently, it restores the expected count of four constraints, corresponding to the anticipated two degrees of freedom for a massless spin-2 field. This new gauge condition facilitates a straightforward rederivation of the gravitational wave equation within a harmonic gauge framework.

Recent advances in polyp characterization using deep learning have been promising, yet they struggle to accurately classify intraluminal structures. Existing methods have shown limited improvement due to the inherent nature of these structures. In this study, we propose an innovative approach called Intraluminal Feature Reconstruction (IFR) to enhance their recognition. The core idea of IFR is to leverage the inherent symmetry of intraluminal structures to reconstruct missing features and use them to enrich the incomplete representations. The water content in pyroxene may be a mixture of solar wind, cometary material, and endogenous water. The heavy hydrogen isotopic and water findings in NWA 7625 anorthosite are significant as they are among the highest in terrestrial planets and moon rocks, indicating a high water content on the parent body of NWA 7625.

, we examine the production of a scalar particle associated with the Higgs boson, as well as its interaction with itself, at hadron colliders. These processes offer constraints on key features of a hidden sector that may be independent of those responsible for generating fermion masses. We highlight specific signs that could indicate a low-energy hidden sector and propose targeted experiments to do so. These include precision Higgs boson studies at next-generation e+e- colliders, as well as production of hidden sector particles alongside the Higgs boson at future e+e- and hadron colliders. We find that, even with improved LHC data, a strict upper limit of BR(s-s-h) < 3.6 × 10^(-4) at 95% confidence level can be achieved with 2 ab^(-1) of integrated luminosity, whereas an even higher precision of BR(s-s-h) = 6.9 × 10^(-5) can be achieved with 3 ab^(-1) of integrated luminosity at a future 50 GeV Higgs factory like the FCC-ee or ILC. We also propose targeted experiments to do so.
